Text
Matching the Topic. The narrative describes Lena planning an unconventional mountain‑village holiday instead of a typical beach trip, which is exactly “a story about an unusual holiday trip.” No irrelevant material is introduced. 4/5
Logic & Commonsense. The events are plausible (making cheese, meeting a farmer, collecting eggs). The only minor oddity is the father being “scared of the big cow” while the mother calls it “adventurous,” which is acceptable. No clear logical contradictions. 5/5
Vocabulary & Grammar. The passage is well‑written; only a tiny stylistic issue (“attractive and fun” could be “attractive and fun‑filled”) but no grammar or spelling errors. 5/5
---
Q1
Logic & Commonsense. The question asks why the parents were nervous, which is directly stated; the answer options are reasonable and none are absurd. 5/5
Vocabulary & Grammar. The question and all four options are grammatically correct and clearly worded. 5/5
Text-Based Answerability. The correct answer is explicitly given in the sentence “they didn’t like strange places.” 5/5
Reading Dependency. Without the text, a test‑taker could guess that “strange places” might cause nervousness, but the specific wording is not obvious; the text is needed for certainty. 4/5
Answer Unambiguity. Only one option matches the text; the other three are not supported. 5/5
Distractor Plausibility. The distractors (long journey, cost, Lena’s intelligence) are plausible reasons for nervousness in real life, so a reader who missed the detail could be misled. 4/5
Using Paraphrases. The correct answer (“They didn’t like the idea of visiting a strange place”) paraphrases the original clause rather than copying it verbatim. 5/5
Explanation Quality. The explanation cites the exact sentence for the correct answer and explains why each distractor is unsupported. 5/5
---
Q2
Logic & Commonsense. The question is reasonable; the correct answer reflects the idea of laziness, and the distractors (fear, dirt, politeness) are logically possible but not mentioned. 5/5
Vocabulary & Grammar. All wording is clear and grammatical. 5/5
Text-Based Answerability. The text says “usually lazy” which directly supports the correct answer; no inference beyond that is needed. 5/5
Reading Dependency. A guesser might think “lazy” means “doesn’t want to exert effort,” which is the correct answer, but the wording is still needed to confirm. 4/5
Answer Unambiguity. Only one option aligns with the text; the others are not supported. 5/5
Distractor Plausibility. The distractors are believable reasons for a child not helping, so they are plausible to someone who didn’t notice the “lazy” description. 4/5
Using Paraphrases. The correct answer rephrases the idea of laziness without copying the exact phrase. 5/5
Explanation Quality. The explanation correctly links the phrase “usually lazy” to the answer and shows why each distractor is irrelevant. 5/5
---
Q3
Logic & Commonsense. The question is sensible; the correct answer reflects the surprise about photos, and the distractors (cost, danger, food) are reasonable concerns but not mentioned. 5/5
Vocabulary & Grammar. The sentence and options are well‑formed. 5/5
Text-Based Answerability. The passage explicitly states they were “surprised by all the photos,” so the answer is fully supported. 5/5
Reading Dependency. While a test‑taker might guess that photos could cause surprise, the specific reason is only in the text; guessing without reading is unlikely. 4/5
Answer Unambiguity. One option matches the text; the others are unsupported. 5/5
Distractor Plausibility. The three wrong options are plausible concerns after a trip, making them reasonable distractors. 4/5
Using Paraphrases. The correct answer restates the idea of being impressed by the photos without copying the exact wording. 5/5
Explanation Quality. The explanation cites the relevant sentence and clearly explains why each distractor does not fit. 5/5
---
Text Coverage. The three questions each target a different paragraph: Q1 focuses on the parents’ initial feelings, Q2 on the brother’s character, and Q3 on the parents’ reaction at home. This distributes attention across the whole story. 5/5
